public_rationale: Several directions were borne out: hallucinations persisted, providers introduced cheaper offerings, and enterprises used competing models. That does not establish seven successes out of seven. The model count, breakthrough threshold, lasting adoption and industry profit distribution remain unsettled. Adoption evidence includes both real deployment and limited intensity; it cannot fairly be reduced to either no adoption or universal adoption. No industry profit conclusion follows from one developer's losses. The evidence therefore does not justify either affirming all seven or declaring the assertion false.

from_speaker: the economics would be problematic, in multiple ways
All 7 of these economic predictions have held strong.
our_interpretation: The referenced list is the March 10, 2024 tweet. Its original deadline was the end of 2024, but this claim assesses developments already observed by December 11.

The seven propositions concern approximately seven to ten GPT-4-caliber models; no major capability breakthrough; competitive price cutting; weak competitive protection; persistent hallucinations; limited durable corporate deployment; and limited profits distributed among roughly seven to ten providers.
Held strong is read as evidence having borne out each proposition by the post date. Merely remaining possible or not yet being disproved is insufficient.
The model count should distinguish substantive models or competing families from repeated snapshots. The original wording does not specify the counting rule or the GPT-4 comparison version.
Limited lasting adoption concerns durable organizational deployment, not every employee experiment or a comparison with the adoption speed of earlier technologies.

Profits ordinarily means positive earnings after costs at the industry level, distributed among multiple providers. It does not require every developer to be profitable, and one developer's losses cannot settle that proposition.

The source does not specify a monetary amount, accounting basis, industry boundary or exact profit reporting period. These omissions prevent a definitive financial score without additional clarification and evidence.
criteria.support_condition: Evidence about developments from the original predictions through December 11, 2024 bears out all seven propositions under their own scopes. The profit component requires comparable industry evidence, and the adoption component requires evidence of durable corporate use.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Reliable evidence clearly falsifies at least one of the seven propositions under its ordinary scope. Missing evidence, an unexpired original deadline, one company's loss, or employee experimentation alone does not constitute falsification.
